prize_parts.citation: for discoveries of the physiology of the incretin hormone GLP-1 and of its active form that made incretin-based treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity possible

statement.case_for: After the full first-round exchange my configuration is unchanged: one part, B003, with Holst, Drucker and Mojsov. The scientific case does not depend on the fact that all six of us ranked it first. Holst established GLP-1 secretion and action in humans, Drucker the proglucagon-derived peptide and receptor biology and the therapeutic concept, and Mojsov the identification and synthesis of the active GLP-1(7-36) peptide. Together they explain why long-acting agonists work. The result is original, independently replicated for decades, and confirmed in large outcome trials covering glycaemic, weight, cardiovascular and renal endpoints. No member has raised a maturity problem. Anchoring the prize on the discovery layer fits the will of Nobel and keeps the achievement within three names without splitting a coherent arc.
statement.case_against: The weakness remains attribution. The active-peptide credit between Mojsov and the Habener group, who are not among the supplied names, cannot be settled from the material available to me, and I have not independently verified the priority record. Excluding Knudsen leaves out the medicinal chemistry that turned the biology into liraglutide and semaglutide, so the prize could be read as overlooking the people who made the drugs usable. Long-term safety of chronic use is still accumulating. A single part also forgoes any second achievement, but I do not see a second part that clears the bar this year.

responses.point: The chair names Drucker, Holst and Mojsov in round 1 after preferring Knudsen to Mojsov in his opening, says he has moved toward discovery over development, and calls Mojsov's priority contested.
responses.response: I am glad we now agree on the trio, and I share his view that contested priority is the real issue. My position is that the contest is between the groups that identified the active peptide, and Mojsov's work on the structure and synthesis of GLP-1(7-36) is part of the experimental chain that the citation must explain. I would therefore not drop her for convenience. If the committee judges that the documentary record cannot support her claim, I would reconsider that seat and, in that case, Knudsen is the defensible replacement because the prize would then rest on the therapeutic concept. I keep the citation worded around the physiology and the active form, not around who first identified the peptide, so that it does not adjudicate the dispute.

responses.point: Perlmann supports the same trio, would reconsider Mojsov's seat before replacing discovery with development, and ranks the unfolded protein response (B043) second as the cleanest attribution with decades of confirmation.
responses.response: I agree that if the active-peptide credit cannot be defended, we should reconsider that seat and not turn the prize into one about drug development. On B043 I accept that Walter and Mori are the cleanest pair on the list and that the mechanism is textbook. My remaining reservation is that its human disease and therapeutic consequence is still developing, and that the PERK and ATF6 contributors (Ron, Harding, Kaufman) sit outside the credited names. A two-part prize that adds a conceptual advance with unproven medical consequence would, for me, dilute a strong single part, so I keep B043 as an alternative and not as a second part.

responses.point: Wahren-Herlenius ranks CAR-T second and BCR-ABL inhibition (B010) third as mature and arguably overdue, and treats the omission of Eshhar as a real gap in fair credit.
responses.response: I accept that imatinib has two decades of survival data and that maturity is not the issue. My hesitation is the one she raises herself: the CML story starts with the Philadelphia chromosome and BCR-ABL discoverers, who are not credited, so Druker, Lydon and Sawyers would be honoured for development without the discovery foundation. For CAR-T the Eshhar gap is real and I could not write a citation that avoids implying June, Sadelain and Rosenberg originated the chimeric receptor concept. Neither fixes itself within the three-person limit, which is why I do not add a second part now.

responses.point: El-Manira ranks optogenetics (B036) second, arguing for the causal, cell-type-specific interrogation of circuits, with a Deisseroth, Nagel and Bamberg trio.
responses.response: The scientific importance of optogenetics for experimental biology is clear to me. Under the three-person limit, however, any trio leaves out Hegemann, Boyden or Miesenbock, each with a substantial claim, and a research tool lacks a disease-level advance of the kind B003 shows. I would not support a second part on B036 this year unless the committee can name a discovery-focused trio and defend each omission.

responses.point: Linnarsson ranks the SMN2 antisense work (B040) third as a clean pair, Krainer and Bennett, for a fatal childhood disease.
responses.response: I gave this one extra scrutiny because splicing is my own field and I do not want familiarity to raise it. The pair is clean and the clinical effect is real. The remaining gaps are approval only since 2016 with durability still being established, and the SMN1 gene discoverers outside the credited names. I consider it a strong candidate for a later year, not a second part now.

uncertainties: Whether Mojsov's claim to identifying the active GLP-1 peptide outweighs the Habener group's claim cannot be resolved from the supplied names, and I have not verified the documentary record.
Whether the committee honours GLP-1 physiology alone or also the drug-design step by Knudsen is a judgement the three-person cap forces, and I may be wrong that discovery should take priority.
Whether any second part (B015, B043, B010, B040) could be defended once Eshhar, the PERK and ATF6 arms, the upstream BCR-ABL discoverers, or the SMN1 discoverers are considered.
Long-term safety of chronic incretin use is still accruing, and clinical translation of cGAS-STING remains unproven.
statement.conflict_note: No change from round 1. I have co-authored work with committee colleague Sten Linnarsson and with Jonas Frisen, but neither is credited on any shortlisted ballot. My expertise in RNA splicing bears on B040, which I do not let raise it, and shared Karolinska Institutet affiliation alone is not treated as a conflict. I know of no documented tie to Holst, Drucker, Mojsov, Knudsen, Habener or any other credited name.
